title: Velvet Runbook Onramp & Toolsmith Adapter: Guided admin walkthroughs and idempotent snippet packaging
creator: Avery Chen
description: Create a lightweight onramp (Velvet) for converting runbooks into interactive, idempotent admin tasks and a Toolsmith Adapter that packages vetted snippets for safe reuse. The goal is to reduce time-to-remediate for first-line support while preserving auditability and safety for privileged ops flows.
motivation: First-line responders repeatedly execute variants of the same remediation steps. Copy-paste runbooks and ad-hoc scripts cause drift and incident toil. Velvet will provide guided choices, pre-flight checks, and automatic idempotency guards; Toolsmith Adapter will publish curated snippets to the admin catalog with metadata, RBAC tags, and proven dry-run results.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Velvet wizard converts a markdown runbook to an interactive task with typed inputs and dry-run mode. 2) Toolsmith-bound snippets include metadata (idempotent=true/false, required-perms, estimated-duration) and appear in the admin catalog. 3) Telemetry emits per-step success/failure, latency, and 'dry-run->execution' conversion metric. 4) Safety circuit prevents execution when a step's required-perms exceed the caller's role. 5) End-to-end e2e test and a canary rollout to the ops team.
design_notes: We will implement a translator that parses runbook YAML+markdown blocks into a typed step graph. Each step is wrapped by an idempotency harness that runs a precondition probe, an execute function, and a postcondition validator. The Toolsmith Adapter serializes snippet assets to the catalog service with an immutable schema: snippet_id, ver, perms, idempotency_hint, test_suite_ref, and canned rollback. We prefer using existing admin-auth and audit streams rather than building a new permission layer.
tradeoffs_and_risks:
- Parsing arbitrary runbook prose can be brittle; we limit initial scope to a subset of structured blocks and provide a migration lint.
- Idempotency enforcement can be overly conservative; we provide 'assume-idempotent' annotations for vetted snippets with manual review.
- Adding pre- and post-checks increases latency for short fixes; keep checks optional with a team-configured policy.
- Risk of privileged snippet misuse: mitigate via RBAC gating, approval workflows, and execution rate limits.
implementation_plan: Phase 1: Parser + interactive CLI prototype (Velvet CLI) that turns runbook fragments into tasks and supports dry-run. Phase 2: Toolsmith Adapter API + catalog integration; publish initial curated set (10 snippets). Phase 3: UI integration into admin console, telemetry dashboards, and rollout with canary group (ops alpha -> support teams).

qa_plan: Unit tests for parser and idempotency harness, integration tests exercising dry-run -> execute path, chaos test to simulate partial failures and validate rollback behavior. Create a synthetic incident harness that replays 50 recorded incidents and measures time-to-remediate before/after Velvet.
telemetry_and_metrics: Emit the following metrics to infra-metrics: velvet.task.created, velvet.task.dryrun.success, velvet.task.exec.success, velvet.step.latency, velvet.step.failure_reason, toolsmith.snippet.publish_count, velvet.conversion_rate (runbook->task). Dashboards: Task adoption, mean time to remediate (MTTR) delta, unsafe-execution attempts blocked.
rollout_strategy: Canary to ops alpha (10 users) for 2 weeks, gather feedback and telemetry. If error rate < 1% and no safety breaches, expand to support SREs (50 users). Use feature-flag gating and gradual percentage rollout for the console UI.
